The metric made it. Queried back out with PromQL.

against the Azure Monitor workspace's own query endpoint — no portal, no Grafana
$ TOKEN=$(az account get-access-token \
      --resource https://prometheus.monitor.azure.com --query accessToken -o tsv)

$ curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
      --get "$QUERY_ENDPOINT/api/v1/query" \
      --data-urlencode 'query=up{job="prometheus"}'

  status: success   series: 1
  {"__name__": "up", "instance": "localhost:9090", "job": "prometheus",
   "source": "self-managed-vm", "week": "11",
   "microsoft.amwresourceid": "/subscriptions/<masked>/.../amw-wk11-dev-scus-001"}
  value: 1

$ ... --data-urlencode 'query=scrape_duration_seconds'

  value: 0.003117542

$ ... --data-urlencode 'query=prometheus_remote_storage_samples_total'

  value: 780487

# WHAT THIS PROVES THAT AN APPLY DOES NOT
#
# `instance: localhost:9090` is the VM talking about itself. That series was
# produced by a Prometheus scraping its own /metrics on a box in Azure, sent
# over remote_write, accepted by the data collection rule, stored in the
# workspace, and read back through a completely separate query endpoint.
#
# Nothing in that path used a password. The write authenticated with a token
# the VM fetched from its instance metadata service because a user-assigned
# managed identity is attached to it and holds Monitoring Metrics Publisher
# on the rule.
#
# `source: self-managed-vm` is an external_label set in prometheus.yml, so it
# survives the whole journey and marks where the data came from.
#
# `microsoft.amwresourceid` is NOT ours. Azure stamps the workspace resource
# id onto every series it ingests.
#
# 780,487 samples. That is the number the ingestion bill is computed from -
# and it accrued while nobody was watching, which is this week's other lesson.
